system.name: IQGS
system.one_liner: Instance query-based Gaussian segmentation for 2DGS scenes; this figure reviews clustering- and classification-based methods and their failures.

content.variant_note: two prior paradigms drawn in mirrored lanes (b) and (c) after a feature-render panel (a), then two failure panels (d) and (e) with mIoU drops; the proposed method is not drawn
content.argues: Existing Gaussian segmentation (clustering- or classification-based) fails when moved from 3DGS to 2DGS or to another scene, with mIoU falling from 60.99% to 35.62% and from 61.76% to 0.82%.
content.subject: Gaussian points rendered to a feature map, two mirrored supervision paradigms, and two transfer-failure comparisons

encoding.color_means: Red = learning signal: the instance attribute I_i, the loss names, the pull and push arrows and the ID arrows; blue = masks and the dashed instance clusters; purple = the classifier; the colours in the renders are random instance colours of the segmentation.
encoding.line_style_means: Dashed grey = panel frames; dashed black vertical = projection of each Gaussian to its pixel; dashed black arrow = a mask supervising a cluster (b); solid red arrow = ID assignment (c); dashed blue ellipse = the features of one instance.
encoding.shape_means: White glowing oval = Gaussian point; blue oval and rounded square = two instance masks; lettered circle = a feature at a pixel; purple glyph = classifier; skewed quadrilateral = a rendered feature map.
encoding.marker_means: Letters A-F name points; numbers in masks and ID 1 / ID 2 name instances, different per view in (b) and shared in (c); percentages on the renders are mIoU.
encoding.emphasis: Red loss labels and arrows draw the eye in (b) and (c); white bold percentages on the renders show the drop.

lessons.what_to_learn: Draw competing paradigms as mirrored lanes with identical boxes so that only the loss label and the supervision arrows differ, then follow them with output renders that carry the metric on the image to prove the failure.
lessons.suits: Motivation figures that review prior paradigms and show their failure on examples without drawing the proposed method.

evidence: clustering-based methods use GT masks to cluster features on the rendered feature map
classification-based methods introduce a classifier to explicitly predict each pixel’s instance ID
severe accuracy degradation (60.99% →35.62% on mIoU) when transferring from 3DGS to 2DGS

summary: IQGS is a segmentation framework for 2DGS-reconstructed scenes; Figure 1 reviews existing methods and why they fail. Five dashed panels: (a) Gaussian points of two instances, lettered A to F, rendered to a feature map, with a formula whose instance attribute is red; (b) clustering-based methods, where mask-supervised dashed clusters are pulled and pushed by a contrastive loss; (c) classification-based methods in the same layout, with a classifier, ID arrows from DEVA-matched masks and a cross-entropy loss; (d) and (e) pairs of segmentation renders with mIoU printed on them, 60.99% falling to 35.62% from 3DGS to 2DGS and 61.76% to 0.82% across scenes. The proposed method is not drawn.
summary_zh: IQGS 是面向 2DGS 场景的分割框架。图 1 回顾现有方法：(a) 高斯点渲染成特征图，(b)(c) 并排对比聚类式与分类式，(d)(e) 用渲染图和 mIoU 展示换到 2DGS 或新场景时精度骤降；未画本文方法。
notes: The figure shows existing methods and failure cases only (the prior merged tag problem-only fits); the paper's own method is not drawn. The caption refers to panels (d) and (f) but the figure has (a) to (e), so (f) is read as (e). The caption says the drop is from source to target scenes, while the figure labels the 61.76% render Target Scene and the 0.82% render Source Scene. The paper text names Gaussian Grouping as the method behind the numbers; the figure itself does not.
